html:
The Julimes were an Indigenous people of central Chihuahua, in northern Mexico, living along the Rio Conchos. The town of Julimes, on the river, takes its name from them.

They appear in Spanish colonial records of the 1600s and 1700s, when Franciscan missions and Spanish ranches spread north along the Conchos. They were probably related to the Conchos and lived near the Jumanos and the Chisos. Missions, forced labour and disease brought their decline, and by the 1800s they no longer appear as a separate people.
